title: Pepper sprayed man died of rare condition
article: A man who stopped breathing after being handcuffed and pepper-sprayed by police died of a rare condition suffered by schizophrenics, the province's chief medical examiner told an inquiry Wednesday.
"The only reasonable cause of death I could find was excited delirium," said Dr. Graeme Dowling. "Excited delirium is a condition that is fortunately relatively uncommon."
Kasim Cakmak, 37, died at hospital on May 11, 2001. He stopped breathing while being taken into police custody at a downtown building where he attended a mental-health program.
An inquiry was called, not to assign blame, but to possibly make recommendations on how similar tragedies can be prevented.
Dowling said excited delirium can cause a person to become more agitated, aggressive and angry.
The high level of adrenaline can cause abnormal heart rhythms.
Dowling said the degree of restraint used by police didn't seem excessive and, if the pepper spray was a factor in Cakmak's death, it would have only been a small one.
